title: Approve an effective, reversible non-hormonal male contraceptive drug

concept.text: Prevent pregnancy through a pharmacological effect on sperm production or function without administering sex hormones. YCT-529 has human phase 1 safety data, but that study did not establish contraceptive efficacy. Proposed completion test: FDA approval following a pivotal couples study with at least 500 couple-years of exposure, fewer than 2 pregnancies per 100 couple-years, acceptable systemic safety, and recovery of fertility after stopping treatment. Test set by: FDA would decide approval; WHO's 2026 TPP supplies the product-development framework. The numerical exposure and efficacy thresholds are editorial proposals. Sources given: [WHO male contraceptive target product profiles](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240124950) ; [YCT-529 first-in-human safety study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43856-025-01004-4.pdf).

page.title: Reversible non-hormonal male contraceptive drug
page.definition: An approved drug taken by men would prevent pregnancy without administering sex hormones. It could suppress sperm production, impair a sperm function needed to fertilize an egg, or prevent sperm from reaching the ejaculate. Fertility would recover after treatment stops.

goal.need: In 2015–2019, an estimated 121.0 million pregnancies a year were unintended worldwide (80% uncertainty interval, 112.8–131.5 million). With typical condom use, about 13 in 100 women become pregnant in a year. Vasectomy reversal requires surgery and can fail. A reversible drug would let men who want children later share responsibility for contraception without using a barrier at each intercourse. Its impact depends on who uses it and which method it replaces. Condoms still help prevent sexually transmitted infections.

figures.caption: Pregnancies expected during one year of contraceptive use
figures.note: FDA describes these figures as actual-use estimates, including incorrect or inconsistent use.

statements.quote: To expand men's contraceptive choices, efforts are underway to develop safe, effective and reversible novel male contraceptive methods and delivery systems.
statements.context: The publication introduces target product profiles covering suppression of sperm production, inhibition of sperm function and blockade of sperm transport.

statements.context: Funding Announcement 2024-100/300 supported discovery and development work on these methods.

completion.title: FDA approves a drug for reversible non-hormonal male contraception.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing approval through a New Drug Application for a drug administered to men to prevent pregnancy without administering sex hormones. The approved use and reviewed human evidence support a reversible contraceptive effect. FDA finds effectiveness for the proposed use, benefits that outweigh risks, appropriate labeling and adequate manufacturing quality.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, New Drug Application review criteria; reversibility is part of the intended use specified here.
completion.threshold_quote: Whether the drug is safe and effective in its proposed use(s), and whether the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks.
completion.basis: FDA marketing approval establishes that the drug may be sold in the United States for the specified use. The andrology societies suggest confirming reversibility in preclinical and initial human studies. WHO’s target product profiles guide development and regulatory review.

milestones.title: A non-hormonal male drug produces reversible contraception in animal mating studies.
milestones.criterion: Mating studies show that male animals given the non-hormonal drug fail to sire pregnancies during its contraceptive action and can sire pregnancies again after the drug is withdrawn.
milestones.set_by: Male Contraceptive Initiative, Funding Announcement 2024-100/300, examples of proof of concept
milestones.threshold_quote: a contraceptive agent in an animal model, resulting in reversible male infertility

milestones.title: A non-hormonal male contraceptive drug is administered in an authorized first-in-human study.
milestones.criterion: At least one participant receives the investigational non-hormonal male contraceptive in an authorized phase 1 clinical study.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, definition of phase 1 clinical studies; the cited YCT-529 study was authorized by the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: A male drug suppresses sperm production or function in a 6-month study, with recovery after withdrawal.
milestones.criterion: Human studies establish when sperm production or function is suppressed over 6 months and confirm recovery after withdrawal. Each product needs its own semen threshold. YCT-529's published single-dose study did not assess sperm parameters or fertility recovery.
milestones.set_by: EAA/ASA, recommendations 49–50 for non-hormonal male contraceptive agents.
milestones.threshold_quote: We suggest documenting the time to suppressing spermatogenesis or sperm function in a 6-month study.

milestones.title: A couples study estimates one-year pregnancy probability during sole reliance on the male drug.
milestones.criterion: During the efficacy phase, couples rely on the drug alone and have vaginal intercourse at least once per menstrual cycle. Assess pregnancy monthly over one year of treatment. Use time to pregnancy to estimate the one-year cumulative pregnancy probability and its 95% confidence interval by the Kaplan–Meier method.
milestones.set_by: EAA/ASA, recommendation 52 and its exposure conditions, presented in the recommendation table.
milestones.threshold_quote: failure rate observed in the female partner monthly over 1-year treatment with time to event (pregnancy)

milestones.title: Safety studies follow about 1,500 men, including at least 300 for six months and 100 or more for a year.
milestones.criterion: For chronic or repeated intermittent use beyond six months, collect adverse-event data from about 1,500 exposed men in total. ICH E1 ordinarily calls for 300–600 people treated for six months and at least 100 for one year at intended clinical doses. The andrology societies specify at least 300 men at six months and at least 100 at one year. ICH allows exceptions according to risk.
milestones.set_by: International Conference on Harmonisation, ICH E1, paragraphs 4–7; applied to non-hormonal male contraception by EAA/ASA recommendation 51.
milestones.threshold_quote: including at least 300 men for 6-month exposure and at least 100 for 1-year exposure

milestones.title: FDA accepts a non-hormonal male contraceptive drug's marketing application for substantive review.
milestones.criterion: FDA accepts the drug's New Drug Application for substantive review under 21 CFR 314.101(a), finding it sufficiently complete. The application contains the nonclinical, clinical, manufacturing and proposed-labeling evidence supporting reversible non-hormonal male contraception.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.101(a)(1).
milestones.threshold_quote: FDA has made a threshold determination that the NDA is sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review.

milestones.title: Disrupting the proposed contraceptive target causes male infertility in a mammalian model.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate that the proposed change causes infertility with a reasonable safety profile in a mammalian model. Genetic loss of the target can establish this result. For a mating or fertilization test, any live offspring or fertilization rate above zero falls short of NICHD’s validation threshold. If validation rests solely on inhibition of sperm motility in vitro, demonstrate the effect in human sperm and in sperm from a suitable model species.
milestones.set_by: Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development, RFA-HD-24-002, target validation criteria
milestones.threshold_quote: Subfertility as defined in this FOA is the generation of live animals from in vivo mating trials and/or an in vivo or in vitro fertilization rate greater than zero.

milestones.title: Preclinical studies characterize the male drug’s mechanism, pharmacological effects and toxicity.
milestones.criterion: Determine how the candidate produces its contraceptive effect, characterize its pharmacodynamic effects, and conduct toxicology studies appropriate to the drug and the proposed human exposure.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, recommendation 48
milestones.threshold_quote: the determination of the mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, reversibility, and toxicology studies

milestones.title: Initial human studies demonstrate recovery after the non-hormonal male drug is withdrawn.
milestones.criterion: After documenting the drug’s effect in men, follow participants after withdrawal and confirm recovery of the reproductive function that the drug suppressed.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, recommendation 49
milestones.threshold_quote: confirming the reversibility of all non-hormonal male contraceptive agents in pre-clinical studies and initial human studies

milestones.title: A six-month human study measures time to suppression of sperm production or function.
milestones.criterion: For a drug that suppresses sperm production or function, measure the time to a product-specific threshold during a six-month study. Use measures suited to the mechanism, such as sperm concentration and total number per ejaculate for production, or motility for a drug that impairs sperm movement.
milestones.set_by: European Academy of Andrology and American Society of Andrology, recommendation 50
milestones.threshold_quote: We suggest documenting the time to suppressing spermatogenesis or sperm function in a 6-month study.

not_found: WHO's final report published on 22 September 2026 could not be opened from IRIS, so its numerical targets could not be verified.
Searches of FDA guidance found no male-drug-specific numerical approval cutoff for pregnancy prevention or fertility recovery.
Searches of YCT-529 publications found no human fertility-recovery or couples pregnancy-efficacy results.
ClinicalTrials.gov pages did not render detailed study records.
No regulator or professional society statement was found disputing the value or feasibility of reversible non-hormonal male contraception as a class.

results.finding: RARα blockade with YCT-529 prevented pregnancies in 13 of 15 male mice.
results.detail: The knockout evidence comes from earlier studies cited by the paper. The original mating experiment measured pregnancies and embryos.

results.finding: Oral YCT-529 prevented pregnancies in 13 of 15 male mice in the initial mating test, with fertility returning after withdrawal.
results.detail: The macaque study documented sperm-count recovery. Mating and pregnancy outcomes were measured in mice.

results.finding: YCT-529 reduced sperm counts below 200 million per ejaculate in all 6 treated macaques.
results.detail: The macaque study used two uncontrolled cohorts of three. The paper reports clinical pathology and selected toxicology screens, with limited evidence on systemic toxicity at the proposed human exposure.

results.finding: Male mice given TDI-11861 sired zero pregnancies in 52 pairings during acute sAC inhibition.
results.detail: The verdict applies to the 0.5–2.5 hour pairing window. Pairings that extended to 3.5 or 9 hours yielded 1 pregnancy in 45 pairings and 5 in 55, respectively.
results.quote: zero females became pregnant in 52 pairings

results.finding: TDI-11861-treated male mice sired zero pregnancies in 52 acute pairings and sired litters after the dose wore off.
results.quote: 24 hours after injection, randomly chosen TDI-11861-injected males were mated with females. To maximize mating efficiency males were paired with females for 4 days, and 93% of the pairings yielded litters

results.finding: TDI-11861 inhibited mouse sperm motility at 15 minutes after injection (n=10 biological replicates).
results.detail: Limited solubility prevented prolonged dosing with TDI-11861. The 7-day blinded histology comparison used three TDI-11155-treated mice and three vehicle controls.
results.quote: TDI-11861 inhibited motility as early as 15 minutes post i.p.-injection when blood levels of TDI-11861 were 20 µM

results.finding: Triptonide-treated male mice (n=12) sired 0 pregnancies in confirmed matings.
results.detail: The paper cites earlier SPEM1 knockout findings. Its own binding assays and the resemblance to knockout sperm support the proposed target mechanism without establishing causality.
results.quote: While vaginal plugs were found in all of the females mated with the triptonide-treated male mice, none of the plugged females became pregnant.

results.finding: All four triptonide-treated male mice in the withdrawal cohort sired litters within 45 days of stopping.
results.detail: The mouse birth dates imply conception about 20–25 days after withdrawal. The primate mating results support both contraceptive efficacy and recovery, with two males evaluated under each condition.
results.quote: The first litter of pups were born within 40–45 days in each cage after cessation of triptonide treatment

results.finding: Triptonide produced >95% sperm deformation in all seven treated cynomolgus males.
results.detail: Monkey sperm counts trended downward, with no statistically significant difference from controls. The authors identify comprehensive pharmacokinetic and toxicology studies as future work.

results.finding: Twelve of 16 enrolled men received fasted oral YCT-529 in the authorized first-in-human study.
results.detail: The phase 1a trial was registered as NCT06094283.
results.quote: Cohort 1 received a single dose of 10 mg of YCT-529 in Period 1 (only 5 subjects received YCT-529), followed by 30 mg in Period 2. Cohort 2 first received 90 mg and then 180 mg of YCT-529.

results.finding: YCT-529 had a reported 22–40-fold preclinical safety margin in male rats and dogs. Sample sizes were unspecified.
results.detail: The investigators reduced the highest planned phase 1a dose to stay within exposure levels deemed safe in the IND-enabling studies.
results.quote: Our IND-enabling studies with male rats and dogs confirmed efficacy, reversibility and safety with a 22-40X safety margin.

results.finding: Six of 12 men given fasted YCT-529 reported treatment-emergent adverse events.
results.detail: All treatment-emergent adverse events resolved. The study reported zero severe or serious treatment-emergent adverse events.

results.finding: After RARα inhibition with YCT-529, 14 of 15 male mice failed to sire pregnancies during the peak suppression window.
results.detail: The paper cites prior genetic knockout work. Its own target-disruption evidence comes from pharmacological inhibition.
results.quote: 14 of 15 males failed to yield pregnancies after mating for 2 weeks (during 3-4 weeks post-CDT)

results.finding: After four weeks of oral YCT-529, 13 of 15 male mice failed to sire pregnancies in the first post-withdrawal mating test.
results.detail: The mating test began after dosing ended, while the contraceptive effect persisted.
results.quote: At one day post-CDT, 13 out of 15 drug-treated males failed to yield pregnancies after mating for 2 weeks

results.finding: In 6 YCT-529-treated macaques, zero measured hematology or serum chemistry parameters fell outside control ranges.
results.detail: The repeat-dose macaque study used two exploratory cohorts of three, with each animal serving as its own control. The paper gives no safety margins tied to the intended human exposure.
results.quote: were within control ranges at all time points in all animals of Cohort 1 and Cohort 2.

results.finding: Male CD1 mice given oral BMS-189453 (n = 20) produced zero embryos in mating tests during the infertile window.
results.detail: Females were examined for implantation and embryos after pairing. Testosterone was unchanged, and all males followed for recovery subsequently produced normal-sized embryonic litters.
results.quote: In group II, all males (n = 20) became infertile by the end of treatment

results.finding: Seventeen male α1A-adrenoceptor/P2X1-purinoceptor double-knockout mice produced zero pregnancies in 29 matings.
results.detail: Females were checked for pregnancy 14 days after confirmed copulation. The blood pressure reduction and baroreflex changes were comparable to those reported for α1A-adrenoceptor knockout alone.
results.quote: This modification produced 100% infertility without effects on sexual behavior or function.

results.finding: Male CD1 mice given BMS-189453 (n=14) were all sterile at the end of dosing, and 100% sired pregnancies after withdrawal.
results.detail: After recovery, the 16-week cohort sired litters averaging 11.54 ± 1.98 embryos. Serum testosterone was unchanged.
results.quote: We observed 100% sterility in all regimens, with restoration of fertility upon cessation of the drug treatment even for as long as 16 weeks.

results.finding: Male rabbits treated with RISUG (n=20 in reversal groups) recovered 100% fertility in mating tests after the gel was removed.
results.detail: The abstract places 100% fertility at 135–150 days after reversal, while the discussion gives 90–105 days. Both sections report full fertility recovery.
results.quote: A gradual recovery in fertility was observed with the appearance of spermatozoa following vas occlusion reversal and 100% fertility was observed following 135–150 days of reversal.

results.finding: Oral YCT-529 had a no-observed-adverse-effect level of ≥30 mg/kg/day in male Sprague–Dawley rats (16 per group).
results.detail: The 42-day study assessed clinical pathology, histopathology, and immune cell populations. The reported ≥40-fold margin compares the highest tested rat dose with the lowest effective rat dose.
results.quote:
the no-observed-adverse-effect
level (NOAEL) was ≥30 mg/kg/day.

results.finding: In four male rhesus macaques given high-dose IV EP055, sperm motility fell to about 20% of pretreatment levels within six hours.
results.detail: The lower-dose response varied across animals. The study measured sperm motility as a surrogate for contraceptive efficacy, and sperm velocity took longer to recover than percent motility.
results.quote: After high dose administration, sperm motility fell to approximately 20% of pretreatment levels within 6 hours post-infusion;

results.finding: Silodosin reversibly reduced fertility in male rats (sample size unreported) at 20 mg/kg/day.
results.detail: The review reports no fertility effect at 6 mg/kg/day. Separate studies at much higher exposures found reduced sperm count and viability and changes in the testes and epididymides.
results.quote:
Treatment of male rats with silodosin for 15 days resulted in decreased fertility at the
high dose of20 mg/kg/day (about twice the exposure of the maximum recommended
human dose via AUC) which was reversible following a two week recovery period.

results.finding: In a Phase I study, all 38 male volunteers received styrene maleic anhydride injections into both vasa deferentia.
results.detail: The text identifies the study as Phase I but gives no ethics or regulatory authorization.
results.quote: Phase I clinical trial was therefore undertaken on 38 male volunteers giving varying doses of SMA, ranging between 5 mg and 140 mg, into each vas deferens.

results.finding: In a pilot study of 63 men, silodosin 8 mg caused reversible absence of sperm in the ejaculate.
results.quote: The study period was January 2017 to December 2017 with sample size 63. Reversible azoospermia was noted following silodosin intake during the first part of the study.

results.finding: Among 63 men enrolled in the on-demand silodosin couples pilot, 0 unintended pregnancies were reported during the one-year efficacy phase.
results.detail: Four participants were lost to follow-up. The abstract does not give their follow-up times or a time-to-pregnancy analysis.
results.quote: During the second part, no untended pregnancy was reported.

results.finding: More than 4,000 healthy men took gossypol for more than six months.
results.detail: The source provides no count of men treated for one year and does not specify the doses or how many men were assessed for adverse events.
results.quote: Over 4,000 healthy men have been on gossypol for more than 6 months.

It could suppress sperm production, impair a sperm function needed to fertilize an egg, or prevent sperm from reaching the ejaculate. Fertility would recover after treatment stops.". add case "Sperm transport blockade". Reason: The silodosin pilot provides human evidence for sperm transport blockade that neither existing case can represent.
